_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_session: 229 (SkyGrain) — the memory hopper tested end to end: 31 entries cleared, 352 corroborated and held for Sam, the rest on a plain-English sheet
_status: The shared memory table has been tested end to end for the first time. All 527 unverified entries were read against what the project currently holds to be true, one workstream at a time, with a citation behind every verdict. Thirty-one entries turned out to be out of date or replaced by a later ruling and have been retired, each with its previous state saved so the change can be undone. Three hundred and fifty-two held up with evidence and are ready to be marked verified the moment Sam says yes; that one word doubles the tab's default list, so it is his call. The remaining 144 sit on a plain-English decision sheet, oldest first: mostly his own earlier rulings that his later rulings replaced, plus the open questions and wishes only he can close. The table also has a lint now, run the same way the docs lint runs. SkyView is unchanged and still waits on Sam's reactions.

items.text: The memory audit sheet is ready, in plain English and oldest first: docs/visuals/2026-09-05-memory-audit-verdicts.html. Item 1 asks whether to mark the 352 entries that passed with evidence as verified; then come your own earlier rulings that later rulings replaced (mostly the funding model), and the open questions and wishes only you can close. Reply by number; yes takes the recommendation.

When Sam replies to the memory sheet, execute his verdicts from kb/memory_audit/2026-09-05-receipt.json: the held promotions first, then the human-sourced rows he rules on, then the hygiene fixes. One guarded statement per batch, keyed on id, one log row per change, never delegated. Then re-run the memory lint and update the lane file's counts.

Three things the audit noticed outside the memory rows need a look: the nightly cleanup worklist has silently lost its P1 and P5 classes because the text they key on matches nothing on the nightly-loaded table; the student-detail lane file still quotes the figures from before the nightly load replaced the table; and the spelling lint sees only about 8% of CLAUDE.md because its code-fence mask runs to the end of the file.

Your three asks of September 5 shipped in one pull request (#1479). Open the Common Course Reference from the side menu: SkyView now fills the window on its own, with nothing above or below it. The Views menu on its top row reaches the comprehensive view (the map with the panes under it), By discipline, By subject and ESL packaging, which are now one tab with a toggle and a Back to SkyView button. By subject is the four-letter Common SUBJ grain, read off the map, with a column saying whether each code is its discipline's Common SUBJ, an umbrella code, or not its discipline's code at all. React by number, as you did on September 4.

Watch Sam's reaction to the By subject table's standing column. Every row that reads “not X’s code” is either a stray the prefix fold missed or an umbrella code the seed does not know about; if he wants it as a worklist, fold-verify is the planner of record, not a new one.

Five COBI tabs still scroll sideways on a phone — the Dashboard worst, by 887 pixels, then RACI, Budget, Memory and Activities. That is the plainest of the accessibility findings and the one a person actually feels. Several sit in sections the daily rebuild owns, so the fix is in the generator, not the page.

One colour decision unblocks an accessibility fix across the whole suite. Roughly four thousand “no value here” markers (the italic “— no articulations” in the grids) are currently too faint to read — 2.34:1 against a 4.5:1 standard. Making them the normal muted grey would fix it but make absence the loudest thing on a dense screen, which is backwards. The proposal is a new quiet grey (#6B6B66) that just clears the standard and stays the quietest thing in the row. Say yes, or say use the normal muted grey.

The accessibility sweep now runs as one command — `npm run a11y` — over all 42 views in about 100 seconds, and COBI's 38 tabs are found from the side menu itself, so a new tab is checked the day it ships. The problems shared by every view are fixed: the side menu group headings and the signed-out line were too faint to read, three controls were under the minimum tap size, the painting fallback panel failed on its own background, and nothing in COBI respected a reader's request to stop moving things. What is left is per-tab and named: five tabs still scroll sideways on a phone (the Dashboard worst, by 887 pixels), eighteen carry text below the contrast standard, and four thousand small tap targets come from just fifty-four rules — one button in the Credential Reference grid accounts for over two thousand of them. Start with the sideways scroll.

Sam approved moving baked-in configuration into tables. Two to start: the list of sites in cobi_orgs.js (adding or renaming a site is currently a code deploy) and the alpha banner's wording. public.cobi_nav is the precedent for the first, the sierra_guidance row for the second.

The dependency map failed CI this run having changed nothing but line numbers, which shifted by three when a comment was deleted. Rule 2 already says line numbers rot. Drop them from the compared artifact so the check fires on real dependency changes only.

Open the Common Course Reference tab, sign in, and open Suggested merges: the first 130 groups are your May 2026 curated common courses that carry the same title and discipline as a course already in the catalog. Each group proposes folding your anchor into the catalog course (the one with the college courses); where the only match is a single-college course, your anchor survives and gains it. Confirm the ones that are the same course, Keep as-is the ones that are not. Nothing moves until you confirm. The lane appears after the next daily run publishes.

Give the three legacy anchors that carry no seed discipline one of the 146 MQ disciplines on the CSR tab: M-ID HOSP 100 and M-ID HOSP 104 (Travel Services), M-ID HOSP 102 (Hotel and Motel Services). The Z-band retirement folded the other 218; the next pass folds these once they have a discipline.

Two curation follow-ups now that the promote step and the identities-map dry run are built: put the identities map's 1,597 stale keys to Sam as a numbered sheet (re-key 1,369, drop 228) before applying, and measure how many curated discipline values sit outside the official list — a bot cohort wrote a made-up one on a live row in July.

For the live-session banner you asked for (a banner on COBI while you are working with a session, so team members can drop in and observe): decide what link the banner should offer observers — a shared view of the Claude Code session, a Teams call, or the pull request being worked — and whether it shows on every COBI tab or only the ones the session names.

Decide whether the daily dashboard run should rebuild SkyView's map layout too. Today the layout is rebuilt by hand and committed, so the map shows the reference as of the last rebuild while the course descriptions follow the daily artifacts. A daily rebuild keeps the map current at the cost of two files of about 5 MB changing in the repository every day and subject islands shifting position as counts change.

Tell the next session the day Pedro says CollegeID2 has landed, and whether it will be on both student reports the daily pull reads. A fresh probe on 2026-09-03 found it on none of the four MAP views. It is the field that identifies where a student originated before the credit college and the one the noncredit FTES calculation will use; until then the public-upload Yes/No (Potential Student) stands in. The probe is one click (Actions, Discover MAP datasets).

Set the Accepted priority's dials through the Implementation Funding tab (your ruling of 2026-09-01: Accepted at a 25% share and factor 1.0; the starting set Eligible 40%, Accepted 25%, Transcribed 35%). The saved configuration on 2026-09-02 still carries the three original priorities at 33/33/34, so the counselor-verified measure is published but not yet priced.

React by letter to the calm pass and the lead-with-the-table changes on the Implementation Funding tab, confirm the explainer as the one public view (the old public page would become a redirect), and say whether the internal tab should keep showing <10 until the public/private split gives it its own copy. These are NEEDS SAM ③, ④ and ⑤ in the funding lane file.

Build the live-session banner Sam asked for on 2026-09-03: a small Supabase table holding one presence row (who is driving, the session moniker, the lane, a link for observers, started-at and a heartbeat) that a session writes through the MCP when it starts and clears when it signs off; every COBI page reads it on load and every few minutes and shows a slim banner — for example 'Sam is working with SkyTune on SkyView now — drop in' — until the heartbeat is twenty minutes old. It is a new write surface: map it in the governance file before it ships, and keep it internal to COBI.

The standing Common Course Reference backlog, in priority order: build the grouped decision view per subject area fetched on demand (the bottleneck behind every other CCR improvement); give the 2,073 rim courses a third signal from their catalog description, as a gap-filler that never outvotes a title; make the Subject and Discipline dropdowns name their grain; and queue a re-mint candidate when a SkyView move leaves a destination's subject code inconsistent — proposing, never auto-adding.

Work the 73 course control numbers that name two genuinely different courses, 93 of them at San Jose City College. SkyView refuses to move those courses because the write key cannot say which one; the fix is upstream in COCI or a wider key.
